entities.summary: Abū ʿAbdullāh Muḥammad bin Isḥāq Ibn Manda was an eminent Isfahani Sunni Hadith scholar of Persian origin. Born in the 10th century CE in present-day Iran, Ibn Manda is best known for his extensive collection of Hadiths, which he compiled into the widely used text 'Al-Mu'jall'. His works had a profound impact on the development of Sunni Islamic theology and jurisprudence. Ibn Manda's scholarship was influenced by the prominent Sunni scholar Al-Azraqi, and he in turn influenced several notable scholars of his time, including the renowned jurist Al-Qurtubi. Through his writings, Ibn Manda contributed significantly to the preservation and transmission of Hadiths, which remain a cornerstone of Sunni Islamic tradition. His legacy can be seen in the many scholars who followed in his footsteps, including the prominent Hanbali scholar Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani. Ibn Manda's significance lies in his role as a bridge between the early Islamic period and the medieval Islamic golden age, a period marked by significant intellectual and cultural advancements.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Ibn Manda's works had a profound impact on the development of Sunni Islamic theology and jurisprudence, contributing significantly to the preservation of Sunni Islamic tradition. His scholarship played a significant role in the transmission of Hadiths, which remain a cornerstone of Sunni Islamic tradition.
